why: The student says t holds the variable a itself rather than the value a had when t = a ran, so they conclude both variables end up as b and miss that the three lines swap a and b.

concepts.quote: Then b = t means b equals a, so both are b.
concepts.why: Because t = a copied a's old value, b = t gives b that old value. The student's reading ignores this, as if = stored the expression a and not its value.
The student reads the assignments as making the variables 'the same thing', so they miss that t saves a's old value and the code swaps the two values.
The error is about what assignment stores, so it is levelled under assignment.
